text: Given valid credentials and a JQL query, When atlassian_jira_search_issues is called, Then the request is built with that JQL and a capped limit, and a no-match response returns an empty issues list (not an error)
Given a real Jira Cloud site and a JQL query matching real issues, When atlassian_jira_search_issues is called, Then the live matching issues are returned
steps: Set X-Atlassian-Site/X-Atlassian-Email/X-Atlassian-Api-Token to a real Jira Cloud sandbox account
Call atlassian_jira_search_issues with a JQL query known to match at least one issue
expect: Returned issues include key/summary/status/assignee/updated matching what the Jira UI shows for that JQL
notes: needs a real vendor account; not available at design time, not a blocker per SOP

text: Given a valid issue key, When atlassian_jira_get_issue is called, Then key/summary/status/assignee/description/comment_count are returned from the mocked Jira response
Given a non-existent issue key, When atlassian_jira_get_issue is called against a real site, Then a structured not_found error is returned (no 500, no stack trace)
steps: Call atlassian_jira_get_issue with an issue key that does not exist on the real sandbox site
expect: Response is {"error": {"code": "not_found", ...}}, not an unhandled exception

text: Given project key, summary, issue type, and description, When atlassian_jira_create_issue is called, Then the required fields are sent to Jira and a non-existent project key maps to invalid_argument
Given a real sandbox project, When atlassian_jira_create_issue is called, Then a real issue is created and its key and URL are returned
steps: Call atlassian_jira_create_issue against a real sandbox project with a summary and issue type
Open the returned issue URL in the browser
expect: The issue exists in Jira with the given summary; URL resolves to it

text: Given an issue key and a subset of fields to change, When atlassian_jira_update_issue is called, Then only the supplied fields are included in the PUT body, and an unsupported field name maps to invalid_argument naming the field

Given an issue key and a target status that is not a valid transition from the current status, When atlassian_jira_transition_issue is called, Then the error response lists the transitions that are actually available
Given an issue key and a valid target status, When atlassian_jira_transition_issue is called against a real site, Then the issue moves to that status
steps: Call atlassian_jira_transition_issue with a real issue key and a status reachable from its current state
Reload the issue in the Jira UI
expect: The issue's status in Jira matches the requested target status

text: Given an issue key and comment text, When atlassian_jira_add_comment is called, Then the comment body is posted to Jira and the returned comment id is surfaced
When atlassian_jira_list_projects is called with no filter, Then the mocked project list response is mapped to key/name/project type for every project
Given a CQL query, When atlassian_confluence_search_pages is called, Then the request is built with that CQL and a capped limit, and a no-match response returns an empty pages list (not an error)
Given a valid page id, When atlassian_confluence_get_page is called, Then title/space/body/version are returned from the mocked response, and a non-existent page id maps to not_found

Given a space key, title, and body where the title already exists in that space/parent, When atlassian_confluence_create_page is called, Then Confluence's duplicate-title 400 is mapped to a structured invalid_argument error, not a raw 500
Given a real sandbox space, When atlassian_confluence_create_page is called with a new title, Then a real page is created and its id and URL are returned
steps: Call atlassian_confluence_create_page against a real sandbox space with a new title and body
Open the returned page URL in the browser
expect: The page exists in Confluence with the given title and body

text: Given a page id, new body, and current version, When atlassian_confluence_update_page is called, Then the version increments by one on success, and a stale version number maps to a structured conflict error instead of silently overwriting
When atlassian_confluence_list_spaces is called with no filter, Then the mocked space list response is mapped to key/name for every space

Given a request missing one or more of X-Atlassian-Site/Email/Api-Token, When any tool is called, Then the service returns 401 listing exactly the missing header names, and no outbound call is made to Atlassian

Given two concurrent requests carrying different X-Atlassian-Site credentials, When both call a tool at the same time, Then neither response contains the other tenant's data, confirming no global/module state leaks credentials across requests
